records.title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. • Отслеживаете
records.text: During a technical review, I asked to see the training data and validation methodology behind a company's "AI-based multi-sensor classifier." What I got back was a fixed decision tree with manually tuned thresholds — no train/test split, no retraining pipeline, a "confidence score" that was really just a normalized distance metric with no calibration behind it. Here's the part people miss: that's not automatically a bad system. A deterministic, explainable rule-based classifier can be exactly the right architectural choice for a safety-critical decision path — arguably safer than a black-box model in a domain where you'll eventually have to explain your logic to a test pilot or an OT&E board. The actual problem was calling it "AI." That label invites the wrong due-diligence questions — where's your training data, how do you retrain, what's your drift monitoring — and forfeits the credit you'd get for being deterministic and auditable in a domain where explainability is a selling point, not a weakness. How you characterize your own architecture changes which questions you get asked. Answer the right ones on your own terms. #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #AI

records.title: Sarla Aviation
records.text: Sarla Aviation has partnered with Manipal Hospitals (MHEL) and Aeromed International Rescue Services Pvt. Ltd.(AIRS) to build India's first eVTOL-powered air ambulance network - bringing rapid, door-to-door patient transfers to life. This partnership brings together Manipal Hospitals - one of India's largest integrated hospital networks - Aeromed International Rescue Services, specialists in critical care air transport, and Sarla Aviation, developing India's first indigenous eVTOL aircraft. Instead of working in silos, we are designing the future of emergency care together. The tripartite Memorandum of Understanding was signed at our headquarters inauguration in Bengaluru, in the presence of Shri. Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Minister of Civil Aviation of India. "The integration of advanced aviation technology with our healthcare expertise has the potential to significantly transform emergency and inter-hospital patient transfers. Through this collaboration, we hope to help shape a safe, clinically robust and scalable model for next-generation air ambulance services in India, with the patient firmly at the centre." — Dr. H. Sudarshan Ballal, Chairman, Manipal Hospitals As part of this collaboration, the three organisations will work together on: — Cabin and medical-bay design, from stretcher systems to paediatric and neonatal configurations — SOPs for end-to-end patient handover between ground ambulances and eVTOL aircraft — Identifying high-impact medical transfer corridors across Manipal's hospital network — Joint regulatory engagement with DGCA, MoCA, and health authorities to bring certified eVTOL air ambulance operations to India Emergency medical transport is one of the most urgent applications for advanced air mobility. When minutes matter, the ability to move patients rapidly between facilities - without traffic, without runways - changes outcomes. More to come as this takes shape. 🇮🇳 Rakesh Gaonkar Adrian Schmidt Payal Satish #SarlaAviation #ManipalHospitals #Aeromed #eVTOL #AirAmbulance #AdvancedAirMobility #HealthcareInnovation
